threads.thread_goal: Align on scope, key deliverables and roles for the tax workflow project.

messages.text:
Kicking off the Standardised Corporate Tax Filing Workflow Rollout for this channel. The goal is to have a clear end-to-end process and ownership before the next monthly filing cycle.

From the project_pack_ref: Standardised Corporate Tax Filing Workflow Rollout, the main deliverables look like they map closely to A1 (overall workflow and RACI), plus the checklist, calendar, retention guideline, review procedure and training pack.

Proposal on scope for this first phase:
- Focus on monthly and quarterly corporate tax filings only
- Include our main client segments: small companies on simplified regime and standard corporate clients
- Use existing office and spreadsheet tools only

For ownership, my initial thought:
- A1 and T1, T5 mainly led by tax clerks
- Calendar and shared folders (T3, T6) led by 497040

Can you all confirm if this matches expectations, and if we should include any other filing cycles in the first rollout?

Thanks for starting this. I can take lead on T3 and T6 as suggested, and also help coordinate the training pack later.

On scope: I would keep annual corporate income tax filings out of the first rollout so we do not overload the next cycle. We can still design A1 so that annual filings fit in later.

For client segments, I agree with simplified regime and standard corporate clients. Do we also want to include the few non-profit entities we handle, or leave them for a second wave?

From an audit perspective, I would prefer that A1 and the related RACI already anticipate annual filings and non-profits, even if we only pilot monthly and quarterly.

For the first rollout, I support limiting execution to:
- Monthly VAT and payroll-related filings
- Quarterly advance corporate tax filings where applicable

Non-profits often have specific obligations and exemptions, so I suggest we document them in T1 as a separate branch but not include them in the first operational rollout.

I am aligned with focusing on monthly VAT and payroll filings plus quarterly advances for now.

On roles for T5 (quality review and sign-off), I suggest:
- Preparer: assigned tax clerk per client
- First reviewer: another tax clerk
- Final sign-off: tax compliance manager role

We can reflect that in A1 and T5 so ownership is clear. We will still need the tax compliance manager to formally approve the procedure, but we can draft it here first.

Agree with the scope as refined so far. To make sure T1 is useful, I will map the current process separately for:
- Monthly VAT
- Monthly payroll-related filings
- Quarterly advance corporate tax

Within each, I will highlight where we see most errors and late submissions. That should feed directly into A1 and later into the checklist and T5.

On client segments, I would include:
- Small companies on simplified regime
- Standard corporate clients

Non-profits: I will note them in T1 but mark them as out of scope for the first rollout, as suggested.

Summarising what I am hearing so far on scope for the first rollout:
- Filing cycles: monthly VAT, monthly payroll-related filings, quarterly advance corporate tax
- Client segments: small companies on simplified regime and standard corporate clients
- Non-profits and annual corporate income tax: documented in A1 and T1 but not part of the first operational rollout

If no one objects, I will treat this as the working scope for D2 and reflect it when we draft A1.

No objections from my side. For D2, I would just add that we explicitly mention that the first rollout is before the next monthly filing cycle, so timelines are clear.

Also, when we map T1, we should flag any obligations that fall outside these cycles but are triggered by specific events, so they are not forgotten in A1 even if they are not in the first rollout.

Works for me. I will keep T3 focused on those cycles and segments for now.

On deliverables and ownership (D1), can we confirm this mapping:
- A1 and T1: led by 315923 and 48446
- T5 and related part of A1: led by 390807 with input from 104021
- T3 and T6: led by me

We can then add the checklist, retention guideline and training pack owners as we go.

I am ok to take lead on T5 and the review/sign-off section of A1.

For D1, I suggest we also assign:
- Checklist (T2 and A2): 48446 as lead, with support from 315923
- Retention guideline (T4 and A4) and query handling (T9 and A8): 104021 as lead, given the audit background

We can confirm this mapping now so everyone knows what they are driving.

Happy to lead T2 and A2 and co-lead T1 and A1 as proposed.

To close D1, here is a consolidated view of deliverables and owners:
- A1 (workflow and RACI): 315923 and 48446
- T1 (current process map): 48446
- T2 and A2 (checklist): 48446 with input from 315923
- T3 (deadlines calendar): 497040
- T4 and A4 (retention guideline): 104021
- T5 and A5 (review and sign-off): 390807
- T6 (shared folders): 497040
- T7 (training pack): 497040 with input from all tax clerks
- T8 and A7 (top errors): 104021
- T9 and A8 (queries and disputes): 104021
- T10 (pilot coordination): 497040
- T11 and A6 (control sheet): 390807
- T12 (workflow update process): 315923

If everyone agrees, we can treat this as the final ownership list.

The ownership list looks complete to me and I am fine with the assignments.

For D1, I would just note that some deliverables require sign-off from the tax compliance manager or internal audit (for example A5, A4, A8). We will prepare drafts here and then route them for formal approval outside this channel.

Great, then we have:
- D1: final list of deliverables and owners as summarised by 48446, with external approvals to be obtained where required
- D2: first rollout scope limited to monthly VAT, monthly payroll filings and quarterly advance corporate tax for simplified and standard corporate clients, with non-profits and annual filings documented but not piloted

Next step on my side is to start drafting A1 using the inputs from T1 and T5 as they progress.

threads.thread_goal: Design and iterate on the tax return preparation checklist and review steps.

messages.text:
I have put together a first draft of the Tax Return Preparation and Review Checklist based on recent filings and the process mapping from T1. This will become A2 once we stabilise it.

Structure of the draft:
1) Pre-filing data collection
2) Accounting and tax calculations
3) Consistency and fraud red-flag checks
4) Internal review and sign-off (aligned with T5 and A1)
5) Submission and archiving

For now, the fraud red-flag section is a separate block in step 3. I used some items from our recurring error analysis (future A7 from T8), but I am sure we can improve it.

Please review the structure and suggest additions or changes, especially on how we integrate the red-flag checks (D4) and which items must be mandatory (D3).

Thanks for sharing. From an audit angle, I like the five-step structure.

On fraud and inconsistency checks (D4), I would recommend:
- Integrate key red flags directly into the relevant steps instead of keeping them only in a separate block
- Keep a short dedicated section summarising the most critical red flags from A7 so they are visible

Examples to integrate:
- During data collection: missing bank statements, unexplained manual journal entries
- During calculations: unusual effective tax rate compared to prior periods
- During review: mismatches between tax return figures and financial statements

We can map each of the top 10 errors from T8 to at least one checklist item so nothing is left out.

I agree with the overall flow. A couple of suggestions:
- In step 1, explicitly list source systems and documents (general ledger, payroll system, bank statements, prior year returns) so new staff do not miss anything
- In step 4, align the review steps with T5: preparer self-check, peer review, and final sign-off

For D3, I think the following should be mandatory for every filing:
- Completion of all items in steps 1 and 2
- At least one red-flag pass in step 3
- Peer review checklist in step 4

Optional items can be marked for more complex clients only.

From the review side, I would like the checklist to clearly separate what the preparer must tick and what the reviewer must tick.

Proposal:
- Each item has a column for preparer and a column for reviewer
- Some items are preparer-only (for example data collection), others are reviewer-only (for example final reasonableness checks), and some are both

This will make it easier to connect A2 with A5 and T5. For D4, I support integrating red flags into each step, but we should also have a short list of must-check red flags that the reviewer always confirms.

Good points. I will rework the draft so that:
- Each main step has embedded red-flag items
- There is a final mini-section listing the top 10 red flags from A7

For mapping T8, I will create a small column in A2 referencing which recurring error each item mitigates. That should help during training and audits.

Once I update the draft, I will share a link and we can check if the mandatory items for D3 are clearly marked.

One more suggestion: in the red-flag section, group items by risk type (for example revenue, expenses, payroll, related parties). That will make it easier to scan.

Also, for D4, we should decide whether a red-flag hit blocks submission or just triggers documentation. My view: for high-risk red flags (for example unexplained large adjustments), submission should be blocked until resolved or explicitly approved by the tax compliance manager.

Agree. We can reflect that in A2 and T5 as follows:
- Each red-flag item has a severity level
- High-severity red flags require resolution or explicit approval before the reviewer can tick the item

This way, D4 is clear: red-flag checks are integrated into each step, and high-severity hits block submission unless approved.

On mandatory items for D3, I propose we mark in A2:
- Must-do for all clients: core data collection, reconciliation to trial balance, tax calculation checks, at least one red-flag pass, peer review, final sign-off
- Conditional: additional disclosures, complex adjustments, special regimes

We can use a simple column in the checklist to indicate whether an item is mandatory or conditional. That should keep it usable for new staff.

I have updated the draft A2 with:
- Embedded red-flag checks in each step
- A final summary of top red flags grouped by risk type
- Columns for preparer, reviewer, mandatory/conditional, and linked recurring error from T8

For D3, the mandatory items are now clearly marked. For D4, high-severity red flags are flagged as blocking until resolved or approved, as discussed.

Unless there are strong objections, I suggest we treat this structure and the mandatory items as approved and move to piloting A2 on a few recent filings as required by T2.

I have reviewed the updated A2 and it covers the key audit and fraud points I was concerned about. The mandatory items and blocking rules are clear.

From my side, D3 and D4 can be considered closed, subject to the usual approval by the tax compliance manager once we have feedback from the pilot.

threads.thread_goal: Set up and validate the deadlines calendar and filing status control sheet.

messages.text:
I have created initial versions of:
- A3: Tax Deadlines and Obligations Calendar
- A6: Tax Filing Status Control Sheet

For A3 (T3), I included:
- Monthly VAT and payroll deadlines
- Quarterly advance corporate tax deadlines
- Segmentation by simplified regime vs standard corporate clients

For A6 (T11), I added fields for client name, tax type, period, preparer, reviewer, due date, and status for preparation, review and submission.

Please review and confirm:
- Which deadlines and client types must be tracked in A3 (D5)
- Which minimum fields we need in A6 (D6)

Thanks for setting these up.

On A3 and D5, I suggest we also include:
- Annual corporate income tax deadlines, even if not in the first rollout, so the calendar is complete
- Any special deadlines for new company registrations or de-registrations, flagged as event-based

For client types, I would keep the focus on simplified and standard corporate clients for now, but add a tag for non-profits so we can extend later without rebuilding the calendar.

From a control perspective, A3 should also include reminder rules for preparation, review and submission, aligned with T3.

For D5, I would define that A3 must track at least:
- All recurring VAT, payroll and corporate tax deadlines for simplified and standard corporate clients
- Annual corporate income tax deadlines
- Any recurring local taxes that apply to more than one client

Event-based obligations can be documented in A1 and T1, with a note in A3 that they are triggered by specific events rather than fixed dates.

On A6 and D6, I think we need a bit more detail to manage workload and avoid late filings.

Minimum fields I would propose:
- Client name and ID
- Tax type and period
- Regime (simplified or standard)
- Preparer and reviewer
- Due date and internal target dates for preparation and review
- Status for preparation, review, submission
- Comments or risk flag (for example complex client, audit query open)

This should still be manageable in a spreadsheet and aligns with T11.

I agree with the suggestions so far.

For A3, one practical point: can we colour-code deadlines by tax type and use separate views for simplified vs standard clients? That will help during peak periods.

For A6, I would also add a field for whether the checklist A2 has been completed, so we can quickly see if a filing is ready for review or still missing key steps.

I will update A3 to:
- Add annual corporate income tax deadlines
- Tag non-profits and event-based obligations, with a note that they are not in the first rollout
- Configure reminders for preparation, review and submission as per T3

For A6, I will add the extra fields suggested by 390807 and the checklist completion flag mentioned by 48446.

Once updated, I will share again so we can confirm D5 and D6 formally.

I have checked the updated A3 and A6.

For D5, the calendar now includes:
- Monthly VAT and payroll deadlines
- Quarterly advance corporate tax deadlines
- Annual corporate income tax deadlines
- Tags for simplified, standard and non-profit clients

For D6, the control sheet includes all the minimum fields we discussed, including internal target dates and the checklist completion flag.

From my side, both D5 and D6 can be considered agreed.

I confirm that A3 and A6 now cover the control needs I had in mind. The combination of deadlines, reminders and status tracking should reduce the risk of late or missed filings.

We will still need to test A6 on a subset of clients as part of T11, but the minimum fields for D6 are set.

threads.thread_goal: Close on documentation, retention and query handling guidelines.

messages.text:
I have drafted two guidelines:
- A4: Tax Documentation and Retention Policy (from T4)
- A8: Handling Tax Authority Queries and Disputes (from T9)

For A4, structure is:
1) Document types and retention periods
2) Storage locations and naming conventions
3) Confidentiality and access rules
4) Procedure for disposing of documents after retention

For A8, structure is:
1) Logging and triage of incoming queries
2) Evidence gathering and internal coordination
3) Drafting and approving responses
4) Escalation rules and timelines

Please review and help confirm:
- Retention periods and storage rules (D7)
- Standard procedure for handling queries (D8)

We will still need internal audit and the tax compliance manager to sign off formally, but we can align here first.

On A4 and D7, a couple of points:
- For core tax working papers and returns, I suggest a minimum retention of 10 years, to be safe for audits and disputes
- For supporting documents like emails, maybe 5 years is enough, unless they relate to ongoing disputes

For storage, I would align with T6: centralised year and client folders, with subfolders for working papers, returns, and correspondence. Access should be restricted to the assigned team plus reviewers.

From the shared folders side, I can implement the storage rules in T6 as soon as we agree on them.

For D7, I propose we standardise naming conventions like:
- ClientCode_Year_TaxType_WorkingPapers
- ClientCode_Year_TaxType_Return

This will make it easier to link A4 with A6 and A2 when we need to trace a filing from the control sheet to the underlying documents.

On A8 and D8, I would like the procedure to clearly state when a query must be escalated.

Proposal:
- All queries with potential penalties or involving more than a defined amount are escalated to the tax compliance manager
- Any dispute that challenges our interpretation of tax law is escalated to the tax compliance manager and possibly legal

Also, we should define standard response timelines (for example acknowledge within 2 working days, provide full response within 10 working days unless the authority sets a shorter deadline).

I support the retention and query handling approach.

For A4, we should also clarify how to handle client-provided originals vs copies. Originals should stay with the client whenever possible, with us keeping scanned copies in the restricted folders.

For A8, it would help to have simple templates for responses (acknowledgement, information request, dispute response) so we do not reinvent the wheel each time. That will also help ensure we cover confidentiality and legal wording consistently.

I have updated A4 to reflect:
- 10-year retention for core tax working papers and returns
- 5-year retention for routine correspondence, extended if linked to open disputes
- Centralised folder structure aligned with T6 and the naming conventions suggested by 497040
- Clear rules on originals vs copies as mentioned by 48446

For D7, this gives us a consistent baseline. Internal audit will still review, but from my side this is ready.

I have also refined A8 based on the feedback:
- Defined escalation thresholds for penalties and complex technical issues
- Added standard timelines for acknowledgement and full responses
- Included three template response letters as part of T9

For D8, the standard procedure now covers logging, triage, evidence gathering, drafting, approval, escalation and response. We will align with the tax compliance manager to confirm the thresholds, but the structure is in place.

I have reviewed the latest A4 and A8.

For D7, the retention periods and storage rules are clear and workable for day-to-day operations.
For D8, the query handling procedure is detailed enough and the templates will help keep responses consistent.

Next step will be to route A4 and A8 to internal audit and the tax compliance manager for formal approval, and then integrate them into the training pack and A1/T12.

threads.thread_goal: Plan and debrief the pilot run of the new workflow on selected clients.

messages.text:
Time to plan the pilot run of the new workflow before the next monthly filing cycle.

Based on A1, A2, A3 and A6, I propose:
- Pilot scope: 10 clients (5 simplified regime, 5 standard corporate), covering monthly VAT and payroll filings
- Timeline: start preparation next week, complete review and submission by the usual deadlines

For T10, I will need your input on which clients to include and how we want to collect feedback (D9 and D10).

For the pilot client list (D9), I suggest we pick:
- 3 simplified clients with straightforward operations
- 2 simplified clients where we usually see more adjustments
- 3 standard corporate clients with medium complexity
- 2 standard corporate clients with more complex structures

This mix should give us a good view of how A2 and A6 behave in different situations without overloading us.

From the review side, I would like at least some of the pilot clients to have prior-year issues or audit queries, so we can test how A4 and A8 integrate with the workflow.

Maybe we can include 2 clients that currently have open queries with the tax authority, as long as we manage the risk carefully.

I agree, but for clients with open queries we should make sure the new workflow does not change any agreed positions without explicit approval from the tax compliance manager.

For D9, I would propose:
- 8 clients without open disputes (mix of simple and complex as suggested by 48446)
- 2 clients with open queries, where we focus on how A4 and A8 support documentation and responses

We should document the selection in T10 and note any specific risks.

On feedback collection (D10), I suggest a simple approach:
- For each pilot client, the preparer and reviewer fill a short form after submission (what worked, what did not, time spent, issues with A2, A3, A4, A6, A8)
- We also capture a few metrics from A6 (for example number of late items, number of red-flag hits)

We can implement the form as a tab in the same spreadsheet used for T10, so it is easy to maintain.

I like the feedback form idea. For D10, we can define that:
- Feedback is collected via the form for each pilot client
- We hold a short debrief call after the pilot to review the aggregated feedback and agree on adjustments

I will add the form as part of T10 and link it in the calendar invites.

To summarise D9 based on the discussion:
- 10 pilot clients in total
- 8 without open disputes (mix of simple and complex, both regimes)
- 2 with open queries, where we focus on testing documentation and query handling

We will apply the full workflow for these clients: A2, A3, A4, A5, A6 and A8, and track status in T10.

Works for me. During the pilot, I will pay attention to:
- How easy it is to follow A2 and A5 in practice
- Whether A6 gives us enough visibility on bottlenecks
- Any issues with documentation and queries under A4 and A8

We can then feed this back into A1 and T12 after the debrief.

I will now:
- Finalise the pilot client list in T10 based on the agreed mix
- Set up calendar entries in A3 for key milestones
- Update A6 with the pilot clients and assign preparers and reviewers
- Add the feedback form tab and send invites for a short debrief after the pilot

This should cover D9 and D10 from a coordination standpoint.
